draft.title: The tangent graph
card: The graph of y = tan x comes from tan x = sin x ÷ cos x. It repeats every π radians, so its period is π.
When cos x = 0, the fraction cannot be worked out. The graph has a vertical asymptote there, a line it gets closer to but never touches.
In one period from −π/2 to π/2, the asymptotes are at x = −π/2 and x = π/2. Others are at x = 3π/2, −3π/2 and so on, every π apart.
The graph crosses the x-axis where sin x = 0, so at x = 0, π, 2π and so on. For example, tan(π/4) = 1, because sin and cos are equal there.
draft.remember: tan x = sin x ÷ cos x: period π, with asymptotes wherever cos x = 0.

a.q: Which of these is a vertical asymptote of y = tan x?
a.why: At x = π/2, cos x = 0, so tan x cannot be worked out and there is an asymptote. At x = π, sin x = 0 and cos x = −1, so tan π = 0 and the graph crosses the x-axis there.
a.clue: Look for the value of x where cos x = 0.

b.q: The graph of y = tan x has a vertical asymptote at x = π/2. Which is the next asymptote to the right?
b.why: Asymptotes repeat every period, which is π. So the next one is π/2 + π = 3π/2. The value x = π is tempting, but tan π = 0 there, so the graph crosses the axis.

problems.detail: In the last bullet, 'For example, tan(π/4) = 1' follows the sentence about where the graph crosses the x-axis, so it reads as an example of an x-intercept. It is not one, so it could confuse students. Make it a separate point or remove it.

check.summary: Both questions are correct and the explanations are accurate. The only problem is a card example (tan(π/4) = 1) placed where it reads like an example of the graph crossing the x-axis.

final.title: The tangent graph
card: The graph of \(y = \tan x\) comes from \(\tan x = \sin x \div \cos x\). It repeats every \(\pi\) radians, so its period is \(\pi\).
When \(\cos x = 0\), the fraction cannot be worked out. The graph has a vertical asymptote there, a line it gets closer to but never touches.

In one period from \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) to \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), the asymptotes are at \(x = -\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Others are at \(x = \frac{3\pi}{2}\), \(x = -\frac{3\pi}{2}\) and so on, every \(\pi\) apart.
The graph crosses the x-axis where \(\sin x = 0\), so at \(x = 0, \pi, -\pi, 2\pi\) and so on. Between each pair of asymptotes, the curve rises from left to right.
final.remember: \(\tan x = \sin x \div \cos x\): period \(\pi\), with asymptotes wherever \(\cos x = 0\).

a.q: Which of these is a vertical asymptote of \(y = \tan x\)?
a.why: At \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\cos x = 0\), so \(\tan x\) cannot be worked out and there is an asymptote. At \(x = \pi\), \(\sin x = 0\) and \(\cos x = -1\), so \(\tan \pi = 0\) and the graph crosses the x-axis there.
a.clue: Look for the value of \(x\) where \(\cos x = 0\).

b.q: The graph of \(y = \tan x\) has a vertical asymptote at \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\). Which is the next asymptote to the right?
b.why: Asymptotes repeat every period, which is \(\pi\). So the next one is \(\frac{\pi}{2} + \pi = \frac{3\pi}{2}\). The value \(x = \pi\) is tempting, but \(\tan \pi = 0\) there, so the graph crosses the axis.
